description: Phase-OUT — Output discipline + budget enforcement. 9 atomic stories (6 output discipline + 3 budget enforcement) backed by 2026 production evidence: nanobot/codex/elysia + arXiv 2511.17006 BATS benchmark + Sattyam Jain $47K postmortem + Hermes ChatCompletionHelper. Plan: .planning/post-drift-2026-05-21/Phase-OUT/plan.md. Live evidence motivating budget stories: 2026-05-22 log elapsed_ms=179668 llm_calls=28 tool_calls=33 delivered=false (agent thrash 30+ web_search/fetch). Phase-TOOL killed the immediate trigger (tool RAG); Phase-OUT installs the floor at runtime-supervisor layer. Per-module deep refactor on touch is mandatory per CLAUDE.md.

userStories.title: Centralized truncate-middle + exec output wrapper
userStories.description: Centralize byte-budget truncation. New internal/agent/tools/truncate.go exports TruncateMiddle(s string, maxBytes int) string — UTF-8-safe walk of char_indices for prefix_end + suffix_start, inserts '…N tokens truncated…' marker the model recognizes (not silent). Add a token-variant TruncateMiddleByTokens for token-budgeted callers. Swap internal/agent/executor.go::limitToolContent (currently line ~99) to call TruncateMiddle. Add structural wrapper for exec/file tool output so model sees `Exit code:`, `Wall time:`, `Total output lines:`, `Output:` framing even when body is gutted (model still gets structural signal). Source pattern: Codex core/src/utils/string/src/truncate.rs:7-69 + core/src/tools/mod.rs:64-89.

userStories.title: Repeated external-lookup throttle — 2-strike hash-based dedup
userStories.description: Per-turn signature counter for web_search (by query, lowercased+trimmed), web_fetch (by URL), and search_memory (by query). After 2 hits of the same target in a single turn, short-circuit the 3rd call with a hard error: 'Error: repeated external lookup blocked. Use the results you already have to answer, or try a meaningfully different source.' The error is fed back as the tool result so the LLM sees it. Constant: _MAX_REPEAT_EXTERNAL_LOOKUPS = 2. Counter resets per turn (NOT per session). Source: nanobot utils/runtime.py:68-102. Kills the 30-web_search thrash pattern (2026-05-22 evidence: 33 tool_calls with 4 ignored 404s).
acceptanceCriteria: New internal/agent/governance/repeated_lookup.go exports a per-turn signature-counter with MaxRepeats=2 default

Probe: search_memory with same query — same shape
Test: counter resets between turns — 2 sequential turns each with 2 web_search("foo") calls both succeed (4 total) — the 5th in turn 3 would block

userStories.title: tasks_completed_string inline state block — kill 'I haven't searched yet' relapse
userStories.description: Inject a `## Already done this turn` block into the per-iteration system prompt (per-turn, NOT cross-turn — chat history covers cross-turn). XML-tagged per-turn action ledger: `<task_N><action>search_memory("X")</action><result>SUCCESSFUL but no results</result><reasoning>brief</reasoning></task_N>`. Injection point: BEFORE the per-iteration step hint, AFTER the system prompt's static sections. Cost: ~200-500 tokens/turn — only inject when turn has >0 tool calls (R3 mitigation). Source: elysia tree/objects.py:759-798. Kills the 'I haven't searched yet, let me search' relapse pattern.

userStories.title: Length-recovery + ignore-tool-calls-on-length safety rails
userStories.description: Two safety rails in internal/agent/loop.go. (1) When LLM emits tool calls AND finish_reason='length', IGNORE the tool calls (likely truncated JSON → unsafe to execute) and log a structured warning. The model gets fed back the partial text only, no tool execution. (2) When LLM hits output cap with partial text response (finish_reason='length' with non-blank text and no tool_calls), append user-side recovery prompt: 'Output limit reached. Continue exactly where you left off — no recap, no apology.' Cap at 3 such recoveries per turn to prevent recovery-loop. Source: nanobot runner.py:398-403, :437-456.
acceptanceCriteria: internal/agent/loop.go branches on finish_reason='length' BEFORE dispatching tool calls
When finish_reason='length' AND tool_calls present → tool_calls DROPPED, logged as zap warn with reason; control returns to next iteration with partial text in history
When finish_reason='length' AND non-blank text AND no tool_calls → next user message appends literal recovery prompt
Recovery counter capped at 3 per turn — verified by mock test that emits 4 length-finishes in a row; the 4th does NOT append recovery, terminates with error or partial reply
Test: mock LLM emits finish_reason='length' with tool_calls → tools NOT executed
Test: mock LLM emits finish_reason='length' with text only → next call's user message contains recovery literal
go test ./internal/agent/... green

userStories.title: Orphan tool_call backfill + skip empty-assistant on persist
userStories.description: Two history-cleanup operations to prevent provider 400 'invalid tool_calls' errors after history corruption (e.g. SQLite WAL recovery per memory feedback_sqlite_wal_windows_corruption). (1) BEFORE every LLM call, strip role:tool messages whose tool_call_id doesn't match any prior assistant tool_calls. Insert synthetic '[Tool result unavailable — call was interrupted or lost]' for declared assistant tool_calls that never got a result. (2) When persisting to conversation archive, SKIP assistant messages with neither content nor tool_calls — they poison subsequent prompts. Both operations logged for /api/insights visibility (R4 mitigation). Source: nanobot runner.py:1070-1094, :1096-1135, loop.py:1444-1445.

userStories.title: Per-tool-class budget caps (web=3, wiki=20, exec=2, source=8, scheduler=5, ask_user=3, default=10)
userStories.description: Add a per-tool-class budget enforced inside internal/agent/executor.go. tool_class() helper maps tool name → class via regex/prefix rules: `web_*` → web, `read_source|store_source|ingest_source|ocr_source` → source, `search_memory|read_memory|list_memory|forget_memory` → wiki, `execute_code|execute_bash` → exec, `schedule_*|list_tasks|cancel_task` → scheduler, `ask_user|request_dashboard_token` → ask_user, others → default. Class → cap mapping configurable via env vars (AURA_TOOL_BUDGET_<CLASS>) + runtime settings table, with defaults: web=3, wiki=20, exec=2, source=8, scheduler=5, ask_user=3, default=10. Counter is per-turn (resets per agent.Run invocation, NOT per session). When a tool's class hits cap → the tool call is rejected at executor level with structured error fed back as tool result: 'Error: <class> budget exhausted (<n>/<cap>). Use a different tool class or finalize with what you have.' Source: arXiv 2511.17006 + BATS benchmark.
acceptanceCriteria: New internal/agent/governance/budget.go exports a per-turn tool-class budget tracker + tool_class(name) string helper
tool_class() unit-tested: web_search→web, web_fetch→web, read_source→source, search_memory→wiki, execute_bash→exec, schedule_task→scheduler, ask_user→ask_user, foo_unknown→default

Default caps (web=3, wiki=20, exec=2, source=8, scheduler=5, ask_user=3, default=10) hardcoded as constants in budget.go

userStories.title: OR-of-four budget guard: iter + tokens + wall-clock + cost
userStories.description: Replace the current single-signal MaxIterations cap with an OR-of-four guard at the TOP of every iteration in internal/agent/loop.go. Signals: (1) iterations >= MaxIterations (existing — keep), (2) tokens_total >= MaxTokens (new — default 500k via MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS setting), (3) wall_clock >= MaxElapsed (existing — Aura has AURABOT_TIMEOUT_SEC=120s; lower to 60s default), (4) cost_usd >= MaxCost (new — defaults to HARD_BUDGET, currently 20). When any signal trips, set stop_reason = the specific signal enum and trigger US-OUT-09 force-finalize. The four reasons are structured-logged as run_events with the trigger so /api/runs/<id> can show which signal fired. Source: Sattyam Jain $47K LangChain postmortem + Hermes ChatCompletionHelper — production failure mode in 2026 is single-signal blindness.
acceptanceCriteria: New internal/agent/governance/guard.go exports a StopReason enum: max_iterations_hit, token_budget_exceeded, wall_clock_exceeded, cost_budget_exceeded, empty_llm_response
internal/agent/loop.go top-of-iteration checks all four signals in defined order (cheapest signal first: iter, then tokens, then wall_clock, then cost)
Defaults: MaxIterations existing, MaxTokens=500_000, MaxElapsed=60s (lowered from 120s), MaxCost=20 USD
Test: turn that exceeds tokens but stays under iter cap → trips stop_reason=token_budget_exceeded
Test: turn that's slow (>60s) but few tool calls → trips stop_reason=wall_clock_exceeded
Test: turn that costs >20 USD → trips stop_reason=cost_budget_exceeded
Test: turn that hits iter cap with low tokens/cost → still trips stop_reason=max_iterations_hit (legacy behavior preserved)
Probe: /api/runs/<id> JSON exposes stop_reason field with one of the four values
Cost-budget fallback (R6): when usage missing from provider response, fall back to other 3 signals; never block on cost alone — verified by mock test with no UsageInfo in response

userStories.title: Force-finalize on budget exhaustion (Hermes pattern)
userStories.description: When US-OUT-07 OR US-OUT-08 trips a budget signal, fire ONE additional LLM call with tool_choice='none' (no tools available) and a user-side prompt: 'Budget exhausted (signal: <stop_reason>). Synthesize the best answer you have from the context so far. Be honest about what's missing.' The single synthesis turn produces a useful reply instead of the current error='context canceled' empty reply. The synthesis turn IS counted in wall-clock + cost but NOT iter (it's a leaf step). If synthesis itself errors, return the partial work directly without further LLM recursion (R7 mitigation: cap at ONE synthesis call, no recursive finalize). Source: Hermes agent/chat_completion_helpers.py:925 _force_synthesis_turn — production-validated for user-facing agents. Telegram is user-facing → silent failure is unacceptable.
acceptanceCriteria: internal/agent/loop.go extends existing gracefulFinalize to be triggered on token_budget_exceeded / wall_clock_exceeded / cost_budget_exceeded (currently only max_iterations_hit + empty_llm_response)

Probe: induce wall-clock budget exhaustion (mock LLM with 30s response × 3 turns) → user gets a synthesis reply like 'I was working on X but ran out of time; here is what I have so far: ...' NOT empty/error
Probe: induce cost budget exhaustion → same synthesis reply pattern with cost_budget_exceeded mentioned
Probe: induce token budget exhaustion → same synthesis reply pattern with token_budget_exceeded mentioned
Synthesis turn logged as run_event with stop_reason — dashboard /api/runs/<id> shows 'agent budget hit X at turn N — synthesized from partial work'
R7 mitigation: synthesis errors → partial work returned directly; verified by mock that makes the synthesis call itself fail → partial work surfaced, no recursive finalize
Five stop_reasons supported end-to-end: max_iterations_hit, empty_llm_response, token_budget_exceeded, wall_clock_exceeded, cost_budget_exceeded

Post-fix targets: ≤8 LLM calls, ≤6 tool calls, ≤30s, NON-empty synthesis reply with explicit stop_reason mention. Document outcome in docs/quality-bench/runs/post-out-2026-XX-XX.md

Anti-pattern: prompt-pressure warnings in the synthesis prompt — keep it terse and factual per Hermes #7915 lesson. THIS is the story that produces measurable bench delta vs the 2026-05-22 thrash.
